name: Child Care and Early Learning
description: The certificate-level training that staffs Florida's child care centres and Voluntary Prekindergarten classrooms. ⚠⚠⚠ Of 1,017 credentials awarded at 37 Florida public institutions under the child care provider code, EVERY SINGLE ONE is a certificate — no associate degrees, no bachelor's. ⚠⚠ That is not an accident: s. 1002.55, F.S. sets the minimum credential for a VPK lead instructor at a Child Development Associate credential, and a CDA is not a degree.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE STATE'S MINIMUM IS A CREDENTIAL, NOT A DEGREE, AND THE TRAINING DATA MATCHES IT EXACTLY. Section 1002.55(3)(c)1., F.S. requires a Voluntary Prekindergarten instructor to hold at minimum a child development associate credential issued by the National Credentialing Program of the Council for Professional Recognition, or a credential the Department of Children and Families approves as equivalent or greater. ⚠ Florida's public institutions award 1,017 credentials a year under Child Care Provider/Assistant (19.0709) at 37 institutions — 663 of them certificates of twelve weeks to a year, 183 of one to two years, 130 of two to four years, 41 of under twelve weeks, and ⚠⚠ ZERO degrees of any kind. Child Care and Support Services Management (19.0708) adds 331 at 13 institutions, of which only 56 are associate degrees. ⚠⚠⚠ THE DEGREE ROUTE IS FILED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. Early Childhood Education and Teaching is CIP 13.1210, inside TEACHER EDUCATION — 31 Florida public institutions, 842 credentials, 513 of them bachelor's and 265 associate. FIU alone awards 216. ⚠ So the same broad field is split across two CIP families and two worlds: a certificate workforce regulated by the Department of Children and Families, and a degree-and-certification route regulated by the Department of Education. ⚠⚠ If you intend to teach in a public school classroom rather than a child care centre, the 13.1210 route is the one that gets you there, and the certificate route does not convert into it automatically. Ask what articulates before you enrol.

cips.note: Child Care Provider/Assistant — 37 Florida public institutions and 1,017 credentials in 2023, ⚠⚠ every one of them a CERTIFICATE and none a degree. Largest: Broward College 124, Pinellas Technical College-St. Petersburg 97, Fred K Marchman Technical College 93, Tallahassee Community College 81, State College of Florida 79. Heavily technical-college.

Child Care and Support Services Management — 13 Florida public institutions and 331 credentials: 275 certificates of under twelve weeks and only 56 associate degrees. Pinellas Technical College-Clearwater 138, Sheridan Technical College 66, FSCJ 41. ⚠ The supervisory tier, and it is barely longer than the entry one.

related.note: ⚠⚠⚠ Where the DEGREE and the state certification live. Early Childhood Education and Teaching is CIP 13.1210 inside teacher education — 31 Florida public institutions, 513 bachelor's and 265 associate degrees a year. ⚠ It is the route to a public-school classroom and to the Prekindergarten/Primary Education (Age 3–Grade 3) certification; a child care certificate is not, and does not automatically articulate into it.

⚠ Named because child development is the academic discipline underneath this work, and DEP2004 Human Growth and Development is carried at 29 Florida institutions. ⚠⚠ A psychology bachelor's plus the 45 semester hours of specialisation content is one route to the Department of Education certification.

⚠ Shared territory rather than a route: early intervention, Head Start family services and child protection all employ both, and a child care background is genuinely valued there. ⚠⚠ Named because it is one of the realistic ways out of a $34,980 to $38,140 pay band without leaving work with children.

⚠ Named for the school counselling side: early childhood staff who want to stay with young children and earn considerably more frequently move toward school-based roles, which need a master's and a Department of Education certification.
